frontier.hypothesis: Exit (b): a clause-B consumer for loop 2's addend that lands on an instruction target already has. Target's post-loop-2 block reads ctx+0xC exactly ONCE (`lw $a1,0xC($s2)`) and derives both math_Distance3D arguments from it by adding two shifts (`sll $s0,$s4,6` / `sll $s1,$s3,6` / `addu $a0,$a1,$s0` / `addu $a1,$a1,$s1`). If loop 2's named preheader addend q2 is carried out of the loop and IS that single read - with the tail spelled exactly as target derives the two args from one base - the clause-B consumer costs zero net instructions and loop 2 gets its preheader copy, taking the residual to 1.
frontier.mechanism: E-s16-1 arm (c): a preheader copy whose destination is used in a different basic block survives combine, and local-alloc's optimize_reg_copy_1 then re-points the base add onto the copy's destination (E-s15-1). The purchase price is one instruction at the use site; it is free only if the use site is an instruction target already emits. s9's 19-point measurement of this family predates the V1 chassis and routed both math args through separate live-local expressions, so it did not test the one-read-two-derivations shape.
frontier.next_probe: On the V1 candidate, name loop 2's preheader addend (q2 = *(u8 **)(ctx + 0xC); base = (u8 *)(sh2 + (s32)q2);) and rewrite ONLY the tail so both call arguments derive from q2: dist = math_Distance3D((s32 *)(q2 + (slot_a << 6)), (s32 *)(q2 + (slot_b << 6))); then sweep the tail's remaining three ctx+0xC readers (link store block, rec_a, rec_b) independently - inline fresh read vs q2 - as a 2x2x2 grid, and score each with sandbox --disable all. Watch build_insns: any cell at 127 that still emits `addu $a3,$a0,$zero` in loop 2's preheader is the win. Diff with tmp/grind/func_80017848/s19/dis.sh.

frontier.hypothesis: Exit (a): loop 2's preheader can be made cse-reachable without duplicating the loop, by removing the join that loop 1's skip branch creates - i.e. by a control-flow spelling in which loop 2's guard block has exactly one predecessor.
frontier.mechanism: cse_end_of_basic_block terminates an extended basic block at any label that can be branched to; loop 2's guard is such a label solely because loop 1's guard branches to it. If loop 1's skip edge instead lands on a label that is NOT loop 2's guard (or if loop 1 is spelled so that no skip edge exists), the extended basic block containing loop 1's exit tail extends into loop 2's preheader and the redundant ctx+0xC read there folds to a copy - clause A satisfied, which is the residual's structural blocker.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate the legal control-flow spellings that change the predecessor count of loop 2's guard without duplicating loop 2 (s10/s12's duplication = 35): loop 1 as a bottom-tested loop with an internal early continue, loop 1's guard inverted with the skip path routed through a distinct statement block that then falls through, and loop 1's guard fused with the top-block guards. For each, confirm the CFG change in the -da .jump dump (block predecessors of loop 2's guard label) BEFORE scoring, so a cell that does not actually remove the join is not counted as a spelling kill.

frontier.hypothesis: Inherited from s18 and unchanged: naming the cse canonicalisation rule that decides whether insn 89's addend is the original pseudo or the copy's destination (E-s16-2) would turn every loop-1 exit-tail spelling from a guess into a checkable predicate. It is a naming exercise, not a lever - the theorem above shows loop 2 fails clause A regardless of how loop 1's canonicalisation goes.
frontier.mechanism: cse.c canonicalises a register operand to qty_first_reg[reg_qty[regno]] (canon_reg); qty_first_reg can MOVE when a class member is invalidated (delete_reg_equiv / invalidate), and insert / merge_equiv_classes decides membership order. The candidate's tail `p = q;` and cell E2's tail `p = *(u8 **)(ctx + 0xC);` differ only in whether reg79 is re-set from a class member or from a MEM, and that single difference decides whether loop 1's copy survives combine.
